text:
Logan Cooley has had a week. Gabriel Landeskog was fined by the Department of Player Safety for cross-checking him in Utah's 4-1 win over Colorado, Jack McBain answered by fighting Landeskog, and on Saturday Cooley scored the winner against Anaheim with 1:17 left. Utah's Liam O'Brien, quoted by the Denver Post's Corey Masisak: "If you touch any of our top guys, me and the boys are coming for you." Cooley has 14 points in his last 10 games, and our numbers call it earned, though he is due to cool a little.

The Mammoth arrive in Winnipeg as one of the league's better teams that the standings haven't caught up with. They have taken 57% of the expected goals at five on five (expected goals measure the quality of chances), and they won the chance battle in all five of their last five games while going 2-1-2. The gap is finishing and goaltending: 4.6 goals fewer than their chances usually produce, and Karel Vejmelka at 6.3 goals below expected with a .869 save percentage. Dylan Guenther and Nick Schmaltz are on injured reserve, which has pushed Vincent Trocheck to 22:46 a night and put Kailer Yamamoto on the top power play. Clayton Keller is off the out list and listed day-to-day.

Winnipeg's story is Mark Scheifele. On Saturday he tied the Vegas game 3-3 and, as The Athletic's Jesse Granger posted, passed Dale Hawerchuk for the most goals in Jets history. The team around him is winning more than it controls play: 47% of the expected goals at five on five and 26 points against the 24 their chances would suggest. Stuart Skinner, projected to start, sits at 1.7 goals above expected.

Our numbers have it close, 3.46 expected goals for Utah and 3.31 for Winnipeg. Utah takes 4.7 penalties a game, which matters against a Jets team with Kyle Connor, at 46% to score, and Scheifele on the top unit. Our sleeper is Yamamoto, at 50% for a point with his minutes up. Utah's playoff chances sit at 70%, Winnipeg's at 27%.
headline: Cooley, the Avalanche feud and a record in Winnipeg
